title: Question and hypothesis

blocks.heading: Question and hypothesis
blocks.text: A research question asks what the enquiry will investigate; a hypothesis predicts a testable relationship or outcome. “Do longer routes accompany lower attendance?” is a question; “Longer routes accompany lower attendance” is a hypothesis. Evidence may challenge either expectation.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Hypothesis
blocks.text: A hypothesis is a tentative, testable statement about a relationship or outcome that evidence can support or challenge. Specify measurable variables and scope. A claim so vague that no observation could challenge it is unsuitable.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Research question
blocks.text: A research question is a focused question that the enquiry seeks to answer using evidence. It need not predict the answer. Its wording should guide variables, participants and method.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Worked enquiry connection
blocks.text: For an invented study, the question is whether sites farther from a collection depot have more uncollected containers during the same week. A testable hypothesis predicts that association. Distance and counts must be defined and collected consistently. An observed association could support the hypothesis without proving distance caused the missed collections.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated
